package_info.why_malicious: These packages are malicious because they are mass-produced with the sole purpose of luring users to phishing and scam websites via links embedded in their README.md files. The packages do not provide legitimate software functionality and are designed to profit from referral rewards and potentially steal user information through phishing.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package README (on npmjs.com or after installation), the README displays a link to a shortened URL (tinybit.cc) that redirects to a phishing website, leading to further redirects and ultimately to eCommerce sites with referral IDs.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The README contains a link to a URL shortener that leads to a phishing site, which is not expected in legitimate package documentation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages use README.md to document usage, installation, and features, not to direct users to unrelated external sites, especially via URL shorteners.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may link to documentation or project websites, but not to unrelated eBook downloads or through obfuscated/shortened URLs.
key_indicators: No actual package functionality—README is the only content

attack_chain.action: User discovers or is lured to the malicious NPM package and views the README.md file.
attack_chain.leads_to: User clicks the phishing link in the README.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the shortened URL, which redirects to a counterfeit eBook download site (pdflivres[.]com).
attack_chain.leads_to: User is prompted to download an eBook and solve a captcha.

attack_chain.action: User is subjected to multiple redirects, captchas, and invasive ads, increasing engagement and exposure.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is eventually redirected to eCommerce sites with referral IDs.

attack_chain.action: If the user makes a purchase on the eCommerce site, the attacker receives referral rewards.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker profits from referral program; user may also be phished for credentials or personal information.

behavioral_signatures: README.md files containing shortened URLs (e.g., tinybit.cc, bit.ly, etc.)
README.md links redirecting to unrelated or suspicious domains
Packages with no functional code, only documentation with external links
Mass publication of similarly named packages with near-identical README content
file_indicators: README.md with links to tinybit.cc or other URL shorteners
Packages lacking index.js or main code files
network_indicators: Redirect chains leading to pdflivres[.]com and other phishing domains
Final redirects to eCommerce sites with referral parameters
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan newly published NPM packages for README.md files containing shortened URLs or links to known phishing domains. Flag packages with no functional code or with auto-generated names and descriptions. Monitor for mass publication patterns from new or low-reputation accounts. Track outbound traffic from documentation links to URL shorteners and known phishing domains.
